description: This horizontal bar chart, titled “Deceived,” illustrates the number of conversations categorized by type of interaction and the extent to which participants were deceived, as defined by a legend indicating red bars for “Yes” and yellow bars for “Partially.” The vertical axis lists four categories of interactions: “Academic Collaboration,” “Recruitment,” “Academic Funding,” and “Journalism,” presented in descending order of the total length of their corresponding bars. The horizontal axis is labeled “Number of Conversations” and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 60, with tick marks at intervals of 10. For “Academic Collaboration,” the red bar (“Yes”) extends to approximately 36, the yellow bar (“Partially”) to approximately 27, and the green bar (“No”) to approximately 7. For “Recruitment,” the red bar (“Yes”) extends to approximately 38, the yellow bar (“Partially”) to approximately 24, and the green bar (“No”) to approximately 7. For “Academic Funding,” the red bar (“Yes”) extends to approximately 64, the yellow bar (“Partially”) to approximately 5, and the green bar (“No”) to approximately 4. For “Journalism,” the red bar (“Yes”) extends to approximately 15, the yellow bar (“Partially”) to approximately 48, and the green bar (“No”) to approximately 7. The bars are grouped by category along the vertical axis, with each group containing three bars representing the three levels of deception. The chart does not indicate any sorting beyond the vertical ordering of categories based on the total bar length, and no bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, or outlining.
